key_insight: Stacking ensembles outperformed the multitask neural network for all three welding properties, with the largest improvement in ultimate tensile strength (UTS).
engineering_relevance: Predicting UTS, weld hardness, and heat-affected-zone (HAZ) hardness can support welding process assessment and structural integrity decisions.
method: Compared multitask neural networks with stacking ensemble learning on a shared dataset.
Used shared neural representations with task-specific outputs for multitask prediction.
Evaluated each property using RMSE and R².
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved R² values of 0.9863, 0.9782, and 0.8453 for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, respectively, versus 0.6724, 0.9215, and 0.8407 for the multitask network.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset size, validation design, or RMSE scaling, limiting confidence in transfer to new welding conditions.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
